label: thm:substrate-parameter-unique
title: Uniqueness of the substrate parameter
html: Given a QOU (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau), the substrate parameter q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) is uniquely determined as a parameter: the braiding spectrum and the positive-definite dagger select exactly one scalar from the Hecke eigenvalue pair \{q, -q^{-1}\} (the positive one). This is parameter uniqueness — the extraction procedure is canonical, with no ambiguity or choice. It does not mean q takes a single value. The substrate parameter is a field q \colon M \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} that varies across the manifold and with energy scale; high-energy processes see a different q than low-energy ones. The observed value q_0 at our location and energy is empirical.
